summary: Live HTTP broker-gateway publisher adapter for transactional outbox transport plans.
claim_boundary: Local HTTP broker-gateway publish seam only. This slice serializes deterministic outbox transport-plan metadata, performs a real blocking TCP HTTP/1.1 POST to a configured broker-gateway endpoint, validates status handling, and captures broker acknowledgement headers. It does not implement Kafka/NATS/PubSub vendor clients, TLS/mTLS, service discovery, retry orchestration, broker durability, full poller-to-publisher wiring, gRPC execution, database mutation, production deployment, delivery SLOs, or hyperscaler certification.

source_basis.use: Authoritative HTTP Semantics reference for using POST to transfer a representation for processing by a target resource and for treating 2xx responses as successful outcomes at the HTTP layer.

facets.F1_simplicity: One source-only adapter crate uses std::net TcpStream and deterministic string rendering instead of adding a new HTTP framework; transactional outbox dispatch planning remains the only runtime dependency.
facets.F2_hyperscaler: The seam proves broker-gateway publishability over a real local socket before later vendor-broker, TLS, service-discovery, and deployment-control-plane slices make broader claims.
facets.F3_adversarial: Tests cover successful 202 ack capture, non-2xx rejection, unsafe config rejection, invalid channel-path rejection, payload-budget enforcement before network I/O, and local TCP request capture.
facets.F4_api_contract: The public API exposes HttpBrokerPublisherConfig, HttpBrokerPublisher, HttpBrokerPublishReport, HttpBrokerPublisherError, and encode_broker_payload over the existing OutboxTransportPlan contract without changing domain/API/usecase crates.
facets.F5_quality: Focused adapter tests plus the 46-package backbone check/test/clippy/fmt matrix, cargo-deny, license-policy, cargo-prefix, catalog/data-class known-blocker probes, parse/config validation, dependency-seam, honest-claims, and diff hygiene are part of this run.
facets.F6_operations: Configuration carries host, port, path prefix, connect/read timeouts, and ack header name, while process supervision, service discovery, retries, mTLS, and production deployment are deliberately out of scope.
facets.F7_security_privacy: The adapter publishes outbox metadata references and governance headers only; it validates CR/LF/NUL header injection and path whitespace/control characters and introduces no credentials, TLS key material, raw message body, database URL, or broker secret.
facets.F8_supply_chain: No new third-party dependency is introduced by this slice; the crate depends only on existing internal transactional outbox planning code and uses source-only catalog status.
facets.F9_testing: Focused tests passed for 3 broker HTTP adapter unit tests; the broad backbone matrix passed 292 unit tests across 46 packages plus one existing ignored metrics adapter doctest.
facets.F10_ci_cd: GitHub Actions path filters and all four backbone service package matrices now include oya-shared-outbox-broker-http-adapter, and all four Jenkinsfiles include the package for Jenkins parity. Remote CI execution is not claimed.
facets.F11_observability: HttpBrokerPublishReport exposes ack_ref, status_code, request_path, operation_id, channel_address, event_id, payload_bytes, tenant_scope_ref, audit_correlation_id, and policy_decision_ref for later metrics/tracing binding without parsing logs.
facets.F13_reversibility: The change is isolated to one adapter crate plus workspace/catalog/CI/task/evidence metadata; reverting removes the HTTP broker gateway seam without changing SQL, gRPC, poller, worker, or domain behavior.

non_claims: No Kafka, NATS, Pub/Sub, SQS/SNS, Event Hubs, or other vendor broker client is implemented.
No TLS, mTLS, identity-aware gateway, service mesh, credential handling, or secret material is implemented.
No service discovery, retries, durable broker guarantees, backpressure control, or production deployment is implemented.
No full outbox poller-to-publisher wiring is implemented; this adapter publishes a provided OutboxTransportPlan.
No gRPC execution, database mutation, SQL transaction, or outbox state mutation is performed by this adapter.
No remote CI execution, load test, SLO, delivery guarantee, or hyperscaler maturity certification is claimed.
